name: Can a landlord force a tenant to restore commercial build-out changes at lease end?

mainEntity.name: Can a landlord force a tenant to restore commercial build-out changes at lease end?
mainEntity.text: Can a landlord force a tenant to restore commercial build-out changes at lease end?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a tenant must restore a commercial build-out at lease end usually depends on the lease, not the construction work itself. Many leases specify which improvements become the landlord’s property and whether the tenant must remove fixtures, partitions, specialty equipment, or signage when leaving. Some agreements require the space to be returned to shell condition, while others allow improvements to remain. Because restoration can be costly, tenants should clarify this before starting a project, especially when the build-out includes custom walls, specialty finishes, kitchen equipment, or mechanical modifications. It is also wise to document the original condition of the space before work begins and keep records of approvals for any alterations. In commercial construction, the lease is often the framework that determines scope, budget, and exit cost. The contractor should know whether the project is intended to be permanent or reversible so the build-out is designed accordingly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Lease terms often determine whether a tenant must remove improvements and restore the space at the end of occupancy. The obligation depends on what the lease says about alterations, surrender condition, and ownership of improvements, so it should be reviewed before construction starts.
